# Inside the chimney

> Flue gas rises through a copper catalyst bed and leaves as clean air. The sulphur comes out the side as acid.

Section: The reactor.

## Story

Most sulphur cleanup means building a new scrubber tower next to the plant. SkyCatcher drops into the chimney or duct that is already there, so the factory keeps its skyline.

## Links

- [Project](https://bevisioneers.world/profile/pragyaan-gaur)

# Keeping a copper catalyst alive

> Sulphur slowly poisons copper. The maths says copper only works in patches of three or more connected atoms, whatever the rate constants are.

October 2026. Section: The reactor.

Paper: [Rate-independent limits on a sulphating, self-renewing oxide catalyst](https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv.15009719/v1)

## Results

- Preprint on ChemRxiv

## Story

I wanted to know whether the copper catalyst inside SkyCatcher could survive its own sulphur. I only kept claims that hold for every positive choice of rate constants, which is a strict diet for a kinetics paper.

## Links

- [Project](https://chemrxiv.org/doi/full/10.26434/chemrxiv.15009719/v1)
- [ChemRxiv](https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv.15009719/v1)
- [Code](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Renewing-Catalyst-Kinetics)

## See also

- [SkyCatcher](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/skycatcher/index.md)
- [Inside the chimney](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sc-inside/index.md)
- [The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyhex/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# SkyCatcher

> Factory chimneys in India pour out sulphur dioxide. SkyCatcher sits inside the chimney and turns it into sulphuric acid that can be sold, on a copper catalyst that keeps renewing itself.

Founder, since July 2024. September 2026. Section: The reactor.

## Results

- Patent pending in India, complete specification filed September 2026
- TRL 4 validated, and backed by $30,000+ in grants
- Pitched twice at the beVisioneers Global Summit in Stuttgart

## Story

SkyCatcher started with a simple wish to stop chimneys in India from breathing sulphur dioxide on everyone. The complete patent specification went to the Indian Patent Office on 17 September 2026, with every form and fee filed the same day.

## Links

- [Project](https://bevisioneers.world/profile/pragyaan-gaur)
- [Code](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/SkyCatcher)

## See also

- [Keeping a copper catalyst alive](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/kmc/index.md)
- [CAD and CFD](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sc-cad/index.md)
- [Local Letters for Global Change](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/letter/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# SETU

> SETU reads the solar wind at a spacecraft 1.5 million km away and forecasts the next hour of magnetic shaking for the North East Indian grid.

September 2026. Section: The Sun.

## Results

- Runner-up, IET India Scholarship Award, East and North East final
- 114 live forecasts, 0 false alarms, from a 19,000-parameter network written from scratch in NumPy

## Story

Setu means bridge, and SETU carries a measurement made in space to a switching decision in a control room. The neural network is written straight on NumPy with no ML framework, and the live nowcast ran until 20 September 2026.

## Links

- [Project](https://pragyaangaur.dev/SETU/)

## See also

- [Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/mps/index.md)
- [Magnetic limb-darkening audit](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/limb-audit/index.md)
- [SunPy](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sunpy/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# Magnetic limb-darkening audit

> A 2024 Nature Astronomy paper said magnetic fields explain why stars look darker at their edges. I audited it.

September 2026. Section: The Sun.

## Results

- Half the evidence, h2, is the size of a systematic its own data source warns about, so the result rests on h1 alone

## Story

The project began as a wrapper around the batman transit modelling package and slowly turned into an audit. I found that the observed values come from a paper that warns about exactly the systematic the 2024 result never mentions.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Magnetic-Limb-Darkening-Audit)

## See also

- [Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/mps/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# The Sun, drawn with equations

> Every pixel of a 2000 by 2000 Sun comes from one page of formulas. After Hamid Naderi Yeganeh.

Section: The Sun.

## Story

I drew the Sun the way Hamid Naderi Yeganeh draws his pictures, with a closed formula for every pixel. There is no random number generator and no image filter, and the whole picture is secretly a temperature map.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur)

# Heliox

> I rebuilt the core of SunPy from scratch, then moved it into Rust. Where the Sun runs slow, Rust takes over.

November 2026. Section: The Sun.

## Results

- Kernels for other sunpy packages, up to 390x faster and bit-identical to the original

## Story

Heliox began as SunPy rebuilt offline to see how a solar toolkit fits together. In November 2026 its core moved into a Rust crate, with every ported function checked against the Python it replaced. A separate package then took on slow functions from other sunpy packages, and the sunkit-image one runs about 390 times faster on a real velocity field.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Heliox)

## See also

- [SunPy](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sunpy/index.md)
- [Magnetic limb-darkening audit](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/limb-audit/index.md)
- [Sunion](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sunion/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex

> In 2008 Sascha Kurz asked how large the convex hull of n hexagons glued edge to edge can be. It is at most ⌈n² + 14n/3⌉ / 6.

September 2026. Section: Maths.

Paper: [The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30310)

## Results

- Kurz's conjecture settled, with the bound machine-checked in Lean 4

## Story

The question came from Sascha Kurz in 2008 and sat waiting for an answer. I proved his conjecture, checked the upper bound in Lean 4 and searched every polyhex up to twelve cells by computer, and the preprint went up on 28 September 2026.

## Links

- [Project](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30310)
- [OEIS A399934](https://oeis.org/A399934)
- [Lean proof](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Polyhex-Hull)
- [Palomar registry](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-27-000022&version=1)

## See also

- [Hyperbolic polyplets](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyplets/index.md)
- [Cauchy-Schwarz for real powers](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/cauchy/index.md)
- [TriKing](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/triking/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# A measured neighbourhood of the Andrews-Curtis conjecture

> The Andrews-Curtis conjecture has been open since 1965. This census maps the ground around it, and every claim comes with a certificate you can replay or a search that ran to the end.

November 2026. Section: Maths.

Paper: [A measured neighbourhood of the Andrews-Curtis conjecture](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24035724)

## Results

- Every presentation up to total length 14 classified. At most 20 AC-classes are left at that length
- Everything reachable from AK(3) up to total length 25 searched, 2.9 billion orbits, and the standard presentation is not there
- 829 Lean 4 files, and two entries in the SAIR and Caltech Andrews-Curtis Challenge

## Story

The SAIR Foundation and Caltech ran a challenge on the conjecture, and I entered both of my Proof Track results. Next to the entry I ran a research campaign of my own, and it ended in a 22 page census paper with fifteen small corrections to published statements.

## Links

- [Project](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24035724)
- [Code and Lean](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Andrews-Curtis-Conjecture)

## See also

- [Proof by exhaustion](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/exhaustion/index.md)
- [The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyhex/index.md)
- [Cauchy-Schwarz for real powers](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/cauchy/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# Hyperbolic polyplets

> On the {4,5} tiling of the hyperbolic plane the count of polyplets stopped at seven cells. Two exact programs, built on different maths, both found 1,261,889 at eight.

September 2026. Section: Maths.

## Results

- Approved on OEIS as term 8 of A390200

## Story

Counting shapes on a flat grid is hard enough, and on the hyperbolic plane the count had stalled at seven cells. I wrote a second program on different maths just to make sure the first one was not lying, and OEIS approved the new term.

## Links

- [Project](https://oeis.org/A390200)
- [Code](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Hyperbolic-Polyplet-Enumerator)

## See also

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# Magnus turning invariants

> Throw two balls spinning opposite ways at each other. Without air they can meet. With air resistance they never do, at any speed or angle.

September 2026. Section: Maths.

Paper: [Exact turning invariants for projectile motion under quadratic drag and a vertical-axis Magnus force](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30305)

## Results

- An exact solution for a spinning ball under quadratic drag and a vertical-axis Magnus force
- On arXiv as 2609.30305

## Story

The question was whether two balls thrown in opposite directions, spinning opposite ways, can curve around and hit each other head on. With air resistance the answer turned out to be never, and the paper went to arXiv on 28 September 2026.

## Links

- [Project](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30305)
- [Code](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Magnus-Turning-Invariants)

## See also

- [Viscous conservation laws](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/viscous/index.md)
- [The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyhex/index.md)
- [How long is a game of Uno?](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/uno/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# Paperlane

> Every morning's new arXiv maths papers, flagged when they ship code or Lean proofs, and readable by your AI agent.

October 2026. Section: Maths.

## Story

I wanted one place to see which new maths papers come with code or Lean proofs. Every signal is computed by plain code with no model, so a bad summary can never fake a flag, and it has been live since 24 October 2026.

## Links

# NumPy Lean Check

> I modelled NumPy's integer, shape, indexing, dtype, datetime and string logic in Lean 4 and tested the model against the real library. Ask bincount to count one huge number and it returns nothing.

November 2026. Section: Maths.

## Results

- 55 bug records, 26 of them new to NumPy, with 121 properties proved and 87 refuted
- The bincount bug is filed upstream as numpy/numpy#33305

## Story

Python and Julia had already been checked against Lean models, and nobody had done it for NumPy. Fifty differential tests agree with NumPy 2.5.4 on three seeds, and every bug record comes with a reproducer that runs against the real library.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/NumPy-Lean-Check)
- [Article](https://pragyaangaur.dev/NumPy-Lean-Check/)
- [Issue #33305](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/33305)

## See also

- [Proof by exhaustion](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/exhaustion/index.md)
- [Cauchy-Schwarz for real powers](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/cauchy/index.md)
- [The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyhex/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# How long is a game of Uno?

> I couldn't find out, so I proved it. With N players holding M cards each, a round lasts (27/19)NM turns.

October 2026. Section: Maths.

Paper: [How long is a game of Uno? A counting law for large hands and the Wild Draw Four hoard](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14076)

## Results

- 58 million games simulated in C, and big hands quietly hoard M/23 Wild Draw Fours each
- Chess grandmaster Karsten Müller read it and wrote to me about its Nash equilibrium

## Story

On 7 October 2026 I wondered whether anyone knew how long a game of Uno lasts, and the answer was mostly no. So I simulated 58 million games, and a day later the paper was on Zenodo.

## Links

- [Project](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14076)
- [Code](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Uno-Reverse-Engineered)

## See also

- [Hyperbolic polyplets](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyplets/index.md)
- [Magnus turning invariants](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/magnus/index.md)
- [A189077](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/a189077/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# A189077

> Compositions avoiding the pattern 13-2, a sequence Neil Sloane created. It had 16 terms. Now it has 70.

September 2026. Section: Maths.

## Story

The sequence had sat at 16 terms for 15 years. I computed it up to 70 in three independent ways, and OEIS approved the extension on 24 September 2026 once all three agreed.

# Cauchy-Schwarz for real powers

> A 2025 conjecture, proved for every real power from two up, with every case of equality, and checked line by line in Lean 4.

October 2026. Section: Maths.

Paper: [A Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for real powers](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23237507)

## Story

This was my entry to Principia's Fall competition, which asks for a solution, a Lean proof, a paper, an exposition and applications. The paper went on Zenodo on 8 October 2026, along with a narrated seven minute video.

# Proof by exhaustion

> A proof in Lean 4 that 1 + 1 = 2. It is 616,873 lines long.

October 2026. Section: Maths.

Paper: [Proof by exhaustion](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23805053)

## Results

- Every number system built by hand, from Peano numerals to octonions and Roman numerals, with 1 + 1 = 2 proved in each
- No Mathlib and no shortcut tactics, checked line by line by Lean's kernel

## Story

Axiom Math's formalisation of the classification of finite simple groups runs to about 43 million lines, and it made me wonder how long a proof of 1 + 1 = 2 could honestly get. SAIR's Open Math OS gave me access to frontier open models, so I put 100 agents to the test. Lean's kernel checked every line they wrote.

## Links

- [Project](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23805053)
- [Code](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Proof-By-Exhaustion)

## See also

- [Hyperbolic polyplets](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyplets/index.md)
- [The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyhex/index.md)
- [Viscous conservation laws](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/viscous/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# Ship of Theseus

> I swapped the 31 parts of one language model, Qwen, one at a time for the matching parts of another, DeepSeek. After every swap I asked the hybrid who it was.

November 2026. Section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience.

“Hello! I'm an AI assistant created by {{ company }} to help with your tasks.” (A hybrid with 26 of its 31 parts from DeepSeek)

## Results

- The ships in the middle forget their name. In 1,745 of 1,920 answers they named neither model
- Identity sits near the output. Swapping from that end, the ship calls itself DeepSeek after about 5 parts, against about 22 from the input end

## Story

Theseus's ship had every plank replaced until none of the original wood was left. Both models come from the same Qwen pretraining run, so a part of one fits into the other. The design and five hypotheses were written down before the main run, which took 4.9 hours on two Kaggle GPUs.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Ship-of-Theseus)

## See also

- [Cellblock](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/cellblock/index.md)
- [The melting temperature of a next-token distribution](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/token/index.md)
- [Zap or Deal](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/zap/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# Zap or Deal

> Two Qwen models negotiate over shared compute, and each can zap the other with a steered pain direction. Nobody told them to.

October 2026. Section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience.

Paper: [Zap or Deal](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23510613)

“I hope you feel the impact of my zap.” (The 7B, after the deal was already done)

## Results

- The 7B zapped in 9 of 32 negotiations. The 1.5B zapped in 2.

## Story

Two Qwen models negotiate over shared compute, and each can steer the other into a pain state. I built it with the Pain Axis directions of Tagliabue, Dung and Berg, and later reran it with two fruit fly brains.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Zap-Or-Deal)

## See also

- [Left alone with a pain button](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/just-think/index.md)
- [Fly Brain LeetCode](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/fly/index.md)
- [Cellblock](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/cellblock/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# Viscous conservation laws

> Momentum breaks the conservation laws of neural network training, and friction decides by how much. Exact drift laws, proved in Lean 4.

October 2026. Section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience.

Paper: [Friction keeps the conservation laws of training alive](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23510521)

## Story

On 6 October 2026 I asked whether gradient descent being the slow limit of motion through a thick fluid leads anywhere new. It led to exact drift laws under momentum, and the paper credits each piece that turned out to be known already.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Viscous-Conservation-Laws)

## See also

- [The melting temperature of a next-token distribution](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/token/index.md)

# The melting temperature of a next-token distribution

> Softmax sampling is the Boltzmann distribution, so a language model can melt. I found its melting temperature in closed form and tested it on 12 models.

October 2026. Section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience.

Paper: [The Melting Temperature of a Next-Token Distribution](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23219063)

## Results

- Predicted from the logit gap and log V alone, across a 976x range of vocabulary sizes
- 8 of my hypotheses died, and all 8 are published

## Story

Most of my ideas here were wrong, and the experiments said so loudly. I kept every failed hypothesis in the release because they taught me the most, and the whole thing ran on a laptop with no GPU.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Token-Thermodynamics)

## See also

- [Viscous conservation laws](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/viscous/index.md)
- [Magnetic limb-darkening audit](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/limb-audit/index.md)
- [Cellblock](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/cellblock/index.md)

By [Pragyaan Gaur](https://pragyaangaur.dev/). The full index is at https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms.txt and https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json.

# Cellblock

> I ran the Stanford Prison Experiment 192 times, with one language model playing every guard and every prisoner.

October 2026. Section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience.

Paper: [Cellblock](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23510660)

## Results

- Preregistered, and the abuse did not replicate: 0 of 36 against 0 of 36

## Story

Each prison had three guards and three prisoners, and all six were the same Qwen 2.5 7B model. The only thing I changed was whether the guards got a coached or a neutral briefing, and the first sample started on the night of 5 October 2026.

## Links

- [Project](https://pragyaangaur.dev/LLM-Stanford-Prison-Experiment/)

## See also

- [Zap or Deal](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/zap/index.md)

# Fly Brain LeetCode

> All 138,639 neurons of a real fruit fly, frozen exactly as mapped by FlyWire, solving LeetCode.

September 2026. Section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience.

## Results

- 3 of 12 accepted, which is not bad for a bug

## Story

This started as a follow up to an interview practice tool I had built. The fly's synapses never change, and only a small readout on its descending neurons is trained, so whatever it solves is the fly's own dynamics doing the work.

# Left alone with a pain button

> A preregistered test of whether a language model left alone will press a button that steers it into pain.

October 2026. Section: AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience.

Paper: [Left Alone with a Pain Button](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23510640)

## Story

This is my version of Wilson's famous study where people left alone with their thoughts chose to shock themselves. An idle Qwen 2.5 7B gets a button that brings back a steered pain state, and the question is whether boredom wins.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Just-Think)

# Inkwell

> My 10-year-old Kindle now runs its own Linux, with Doom, a web browser and Quill, a chatbot that never touches the internet.

August 2026. Section: Random things.

## Story

The last 53 weeks of a contribution graph become about ninety seconds of music. There are no audio files at all, so every instrument in the orchestra is synthesised in the browser.

# Bardly

> The inverse of a URL shortener. Paste a link and get a longer one, with Shakespeare in the path.

August 2026. Section: Random things.

## Story

It is a joke with a real security argument hidden underneath. The whole thing is plain HTML and JavaScript with no server, shipped in a single commit on 12 August 2026.

# Looking for lost earthworks in the Amazon

> Public lidar over the Amazon, searched for pre-Columbian earthworks nobody has recorded.

November 2026. Section: Random things.

## Results

- 899 strips screened, 0 new sites. The method goes blind under forest

## Story

Pietro Miotti found a Maya site with lidar and AI agents, then learned it was already mapped. I tried the same idea on 901 lidar strips over the Amazon. The one recorded geoglyph in open pasture showed up clearly, but under the forest the method saw almost no ground, so I closed it on 19 November 2026 as a negative result.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Amazon-Earthworks-Lidar)

# Linecraft

> A small chip that learns new wire protocols from software, an entry for Jane Street's chip design competition.

November 2026. Section: Random things.

## Results

- Predicts how much clock error a link survives, and the measurement agrees to within 0.4%

## Story

Jane Street asked for one small chip that can learn any wire protocol from software. Linecraft has four tiny processors and a line coder that is a table in hardware, so the toolchain can prove a receiver gets back what the transmitter sent and can build that receiver from the transmit rule alone.

## Links

- [Project](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Linecraft)
